summary: The compat-patches domain has no target-state authority (A-09). It holds 17 live hotfix modules loaded through a side-effect import chain, and this audit inventories 109 live runtime monkey-patch sites across the codebase (feats, compat-patches, progression, talents, force, infrastructure, combat, actor-core), including wrappers over core authorities (DerivedCalculator.computeAll, ModifierEngine, SWSEChat.postRoll) and order-dependent wrapper chains on CombatOptionResolver and ForceExecutor.

responsibilities.responsibility: Load all hotfixes by side-effect import

allowed: none (A-09 target state is zero patches)

contradictions.observed: Wider scan: 108 live sites in 41 live files (static-method reassignment, proto aliases, Document.prototype)

foundryAcceptance.item: Any fold-back of a class-F patch (combat attack options, follower lifecycle, progression steps)

findings.title: 109 live runtime monkey-patch sites in live modules across 8 owner domains
findings.observed: Live sites by owner domain: feats 32, compat-patches 27, progression 24, talents 11, force 9, infrastructure 3, combat 2, actor-core 1 (instance patch of actor.items). Targets include DerivedCalculator.computeAll, ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, SWSEChat.postRoll, DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor, PrerequisiteChecker, AbilityEngine.evaluateAcquisition, TalentStep/ForcePowerStep prototypes, ProgressionFinalizer statics, Document.prototype flag methods. Every live site with its target is listed in dependencies.observedViolations (from = site, to = patched target).
findings.intendedOwnership: Behaviour lives in the owning module; no runtime reassignment (A-09).
findings.proposedSolution: Per owner domain, fold each wrapper body into the target method (or a declared extension registry, e.g. a CombatOptionResolver modifier-source registry) and delete the patch. Order: (1) patches on core authorities (DerivedCalculator.computeAll, ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, SWSEChat.postRoll, DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor, ActorEngine), (2) progression step patches, (3) combat option chains, (4) UI patches. Add a CI ratchet that fails on new reassignment sites.
findings.alternatives: Keep patches but centralise installation and assert installation in tests.
findings.regressionTests: For each fold: behaviour parity test that previously ran with the patch installed; census ratchet.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Every class-F patch: live Foundry run of the affected flow.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes parallel execution paths and order dependence.
findings.risk: High if folded without parity tests; combat/progression are runtime-risk areas.

findings.title: Follower hotfixes write owner-actor flags directly and non-atomically
findings.observed: owner.setFlag("foundryvtt-swse","followerSlots") then a second setFlag("followers") - two persisted writes outside ActorEngine; a failure between them leaves slots and roster inconsistent. Entitlement repair writes followerSlots on ready.
findings.intendedOwnership: Owner actor state through ActorEngine (A-02), one write per logical change.
findings.proposedSolution: Replace with one ActorEngine.updateActor(owner, {"flags.foundryvtt-swse.followerSlots":..., "flags.foundryvtt-swse.followers":...}) call; then fold the logic into npc-followers.
findings.regressionTests: Fake-ActorEngine test: transfer produces one update with both keys.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Follower transfer when owner deleted, in Foundry.

findings.title: Hotfix layer composed by a hidden side-effect import chain
findings.observed: A module described as "Exposes a macro menu for Squad Actions talent" side-effect imports the whole hotfix layer and two progression-finalizer patches; registration happens at module evaluation (before init) and its order relative to other patches depends on index.js import order.
findings.intendedOwnership: Composition root (index.js) calls explicit registration functions in a documented order.
findings.proposedSolution: Until patches are folded: move the imports into index.js as explicit calls inside init with a comment listing order dependencies; remove side-effect imports from squad-actions-init.js.
findings.regressionTests: Test that squad-actions-init has no side-effect imports.

findings.title: Wrapper chains on combat and Force execution entry points
findings.observed: CombatOptionResolver.collectAttackModifiers is reassigned by 8 live modules and ForceExecutor.executeForcePower by 4; each wraps the previous value, so the effective behaviour is the composition in ES-module evaluation order, which no test pins.
findings.intendedOwnership: One resolver that iterates a declared contribution list (combat/force own the order).
findings.proposedSolution: Introduce explicit contributor registries (attack-modifier contributors; force-power post-execution steps) in combat/force and migrate each wrapper into a contributor with an explicit priority equal to its current effective order.
findings.regressionTests: Snapshot test of collectAttackModifiers output for a fixture actor with all relevant feats, before/after.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Attack rolls with stacked feat options; Force power execution.
findings.risk: High: attack math is a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: Document.prototype flag-scope patch affects every document type
findings.observed: getFlag("swse") reads canonical then legacy flags.swse; setFlag("swse") writes canonical. Installed globally for all Documents (also other modules' documents). SWSEActorBase repeats the same remap. Direct writes to flags.swse via update() remain possible, so canonical can shadow fresher legacy values (see F-ACT-009).
findings.intendedOwnership: One flag namespace; migration instead of a global shim (A-09).
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides canonical namespace; migrate persisted flags.swse into it (B-MIG), reroute flags.swse literal reads, then remove both shims.
findings.regressionTests: Round-trip flag tests per document type.

findings.title: Probe false positives and an exact clone
findings.observed: Lines 159/334/212 are Set.delete on in-memory re-entrancy guards (false positives). combat-ui-behavior-hotfix.applyForcedAttackOption is an exact 176-token clone of combat-feature-handlers.applyForcedAttackOption.
findings.proposedSolution: Allow-list the Set.delete sites; replace the clone with an import of the combat-feature-handlers export.

findings.title: 50 unreachable monkey-patch sites in unreachable modules
findings.observed: Feat rider patches, combat action adapters, sentinel hook layers and enforcement-core patch targets but are never imported (registry reachability).
findings.proposedSolution: Delete (legacy C) after owner confirms none is a pending integration; some feat riders (e.g. relentless-attack, sport-hunter) may be UNIMPLEMENTED features - list them to the feats owner first.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes dormant patches that could be re-wired accidentally.
